answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils costly: a new agent joins only when established members lock collateral behind it, like a reef built from many anchored stakes. If that identity cheats, the slash hits every voucher, so an attacker spinning up a sable fleet of fakes must self-fund each bond. A single gale of coordinated fraud wipes the whole stake, and honest vouchers refuse to sponsor strangers, so the attacker's cost scales with every new identity, not with ambition.
